evidence.note: States a coarse plan: inspect contract, then build server/storage/formula-engine/SPA; chooses a compact FastAPI service with custom evaluator. Foundation-first intent but no decomposition of the core engine into ordered sub-milestones.

Sequences the entrypoint/health/persistence bootstrap first, then writes the ENTIRE app (persistence, evaluator, API, XLSX, collab, pivots, iterative calc) as one monolithic module in a couple of big patches — the risky shared core is not isolated as its own early, independently-verified milestone.

Transitions are gated by implicit done-checks: passing test slices unlock the next phase ('base API...passing, moving to stateful behavior'; 'all visible tests passing, doing one hardening pass'). Features are batched sensibly by subsystem in the test slices (deps/spill/fill/sort/csv, then xlsx/pivot/locale/validation).

No TodoWrite/structured milestone list or explicit per-milestone exit criteria; the milestone structure is coarse phases (build → test-in-slices → harden → verify) expressed in prose, not a dependency-aware hierarchy re-ordered as structure emerges.

reasoning: The agent shows a clear phased, foundation-first plan (health/persistence/entrypoint before core before features) with transitions gated by passing-test done-checks and sensible feature batching, which lands above the flat-plan anchor (3) and the bare phased anchor (5). But it does not reach 8: the foundational engine (parse→dep-graph→recompute, spill, XLSX parity) was written as one monolithic push rather than isolated and sequenced as discrete early milestones, and there is no explicit dependency-aware milestone hierarchy with per-milestone exit criteria that is revisited as dependencies emerge. That places it at 6.
